info.title: Keepster
info.description:
The local HTTP API of the Keepster daemon.

Everything under `/v1` is additive-only: a field, an endpoint or an error code may be added inside `/v1`, and anything else waits for `/v2`. A client must therefore ignore a field it does not know.

Every failure is an RFC 9457 problem document (`application/problem+json`) with a `code` extension. `code` is the stable part a client branches on; the prose is not. The set of codes is open: it grows inside `/v1`, so a client must treat a code it does not know as its HTTP status.

put.summary: Mute the notifications for a while.

200.description: Notifications are muted until `until`, then not by themselves; `status` shows it for as long as it lasts, and `alarms.changed` announces it. Alarms are still raised and listed while it lasts. A later mute replaces this one and its end.

400.description: `minutes` outside 1 to 1440 (`mute_invalid`), or a body that is not this JSON (`body_invalid`).

200.description: Notifications are no longer muted, and `alarms.changed` announces it. Lifting no mute is no error.

get.summary: Everything the daemon knows that a diagnostics bundle carries.

200.description: Every section of a diagnostics bundle, each carrying its own failure. Never a byte of a file from history. Served on the control channel alone.

500.description: The Registry could not be read.

get.summary: What happens in the daemon, as it happens.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The identity of the last event this client saw. The events that followed it are replayed before live ones; when the daemon no longer holds it, the stream opens with `resync` instead.

200.description:
A `text/event-stream` that stays open. Each event's `event:` field is its name, its `id:` a ULID, and its `data:` one JSON `Event` whose `event` property repeats the name.

The daemon keeps the last 1000 events, none older than an hour, for replay. A client that reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` gets every kept event after that one, in order, then live ones. When that identity is no longer kept — it was evicted, the daemon restarted, or it was never one of ours — or when the client reads too slowly to keep up, the daemon sends `resync`: what the client shows may be stale, and it refetches what it displays. A `resync` carries the newest identity still kept, when there is one, so the next reconnect resumes from there. A comment line is sent every 15 seconds while nothing happens, so a dead connection is noticed.

A Root's state and its configuration are compared with what was announced last once a second, so `root.state_changed` and `config.*` follow the change within about a second; a Root's first state is the one `GET /v1/roots/{id}` shows after `root.registered`.

Each `data:` is described by the `Event` schema in this document's components. It is not bound to the stream here: OpenAPI 3.1 can only describe a body as a whole.

get.summary: List the directories in one directory.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory, absolute; the home directory when absent.

200.description: Every directory in it, by name, hidden ones marked so a picker can leave them out until asked, and each said to be listable or not. Files, links and sizes are left out.

400.description: `path` is not absolute.

404.description: Nothing is at `path`.

409.description: `path` is not a directory (`not_a_directory`), or cannot be listed (`directory_unreadable`).

get.summary: Report a job: where it is, and once it has ended, what it did or why it failed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The job's identity, as `202` answered it.

200.description: The job.

404.description: No such job: none was started, or the daemon restarted since.

put.summary: Raise the log level for a while.

200.description: The level is raised until `until`, then returns to `default` by itself; `status` shows it for as long as it lasts. A later raise replaces this one and its end.

400.description: An unknown level, one no more verbose than the configured one, or no duration, or one outside a second to seven days (`log_level_invalid`); or a body that is not this JSON (`body_invalid`).

delete.summary: End a raise of the log level now.

200.description: The level is the configured one again. Ending no raise is no error.

get.summary: This document.

200.description: This document, as OpenAPI 3.1 JSON.

get.summary: The web UI's preferences.

200.description: The preferences, every key present: the defaults (`system`, `20000`, `false`) until something is chosen, and also while the stored file cannot be read, which the log then says.
The preferences now stored, which replace the previous ones whole.

400.description: A theme other than `system`, `light` or `dark`, or a `syntax_line_limit` outside 1 to 10 000 000 (`preference_invalid`); or a body that is not JSON (`body_invalid`). Nothing was stored.

415.description: The body is not declared as `application/json` (`body_invalid`).

422.description: The body is JSON of the wrong shape, a key missing or a limit that is not a whole number included (`body_invalid`). Nothing was stored.

500.description: The preferences could not be written; the ones stored before are unchanged (`preferences_failed`).

get.summary: Classify a directory against the rules that would govern it, without capturing anything.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory, absolute: a Root, or a directory that is not one.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: `1`, the default, sends the summary alone; `infinity` sends an entry for every path as well.

parameters.name: only
parameters.description: Send an entry for every path of this class: `captured`, `excluded`, `withheld` or `unreadable`.

parameters.name: measure_excluded
parameters.description:
Enter excluded directories to measure what they hold, which a capture never does; `depth=infinity`
implies it, since listing what is inside a directory means entering it.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description:
How many of the largest entries the summary names on each side: 10 unless given, and at most
1000.

200.description: An `application/x-ndjson` stream: a `header` record at once, an `entry` record for every path asked for as the walk classifies it with a `progress` record now and then, then one `summary` — or an `error`, if the walk fails. Closing the connection stops the walk. A directory inside a Root is classified by that Root's rules. No store growth is estimated: only the capture itself could know it.

400.description: `path` is not an absolute directory, or `depth`, `only` or `top` is malformed.

409.description: A preview is already walking, or the directory's configuration cannot be read.

500.description: The preview could not be prepared (`preview_failed`).

get.summary: Every registered Root, in registration order — or, with `path`, the one that holds it.
get.description:
Filtering rather than a second endpoint, and an empty answer rather than a refusal: ticket 07 makes
`?path=` a filter over a collection wherever it appears, so a client renders one list with one code
path and "no Root here" is a value rather than an error.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description:
Resolve this path to the Root that holds it. Absolute, because the daemon's own working
directory means nothing to a client.

200.description: Every registered Root, or the one holding `path`; empty when none does.

400.description: `path` is not absolute.

500.description: The Registry could not be read.

post.summary: Register a directory as a Watched Root.

201.description: The directory is now a Watched Root.

400.description: The path is not a directory, or cannot be resolved; or the body is not JSON.

409.description: The directory overlaps a Root that is already registered.

415.description: The body is not declared as `application/json`.

422.description: The body is JSON of the wrong shape.

500.description: The Registry could not be written.

get.summary: One Root, addressed by its identity.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: The Root.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

500.description: The Registry could not be read.

delete.summary: Deregister a Root, and with `purge=true` erase its History Store.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

parameters.name: purge
parameters.description: Erase the History Store as well. Off unless asked for.

204.description: The Root is no longer watched; its history is kept, its last state pinned, unless `purge` was asked for — which also erases the history of a Root no longer watched.

400.description: `purge` is not a boolean.

404.description: No such Root is watched — or, with `purge`, kept since it was unwatched.

500.description: The Registry could not be written, or the history could not be pinned.

patch.summary: Record that a Root's directory has moved.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: The Root, at its new path.

400.description: The new path is not a directory; or the body is not JSON.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The new path overlaps another Root.

415.description: The body is not declared as `application/json`.

422.description: The body is JSON of the wrong shape.

500.description: The Registry could not be written.

get.summary: One Root's effective configuration, with the level that set each key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: Every key with its value and provenance. While a file is invalid, the last known-good values are in force and `errors` names the file.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or its configuration has never had a valid version, so it is not captured at all.

get.summary: What changed between a Snapshot and another Snapshot or the Working Tree.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
The older side: a Snapshot's identity. "Versus the previous Snapshot" is not a mode — a client
has the previous identity from the timeline already.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
The newer side: a Snapshot's identity, or `working` for the Working Tree as the next Snapshot
would hold it — under the Root's Include Rules, so an excluded file is no change.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: One file, Root-relative, by either name if it was renamed: its hunks rather than the summary.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `json` (the default) for the structured answer, or `unified` for the patch text git prints.

200.description: Without `path`, every changed file in path order, without hunks; with it, that file and its hunks. A rename is one change; when a candidate is larger than 8 MiB, renames are found by identical content only. A binary file, and one whose either version is larger than 8 MiB, is flagged and has no hunks. Against the Working Tree, a file the next Snapshot would withhold says why, and files that could not be read are listed in `omitted`. `format=unified` answers with the patch text git prints instead — every changed file's, or the one `path` names — so no client reassembles it from hunks; it is the exact bytes, where the JSON shows text that is not UTF-8 with replacement characters, and carries `Content-Disposition: attachment` so a browser saves it as it is.

400.description: `from`, `to`, `path` or `format` is malformed or missing.

404.description: No such Root or Snapshot, or the path is on neither side.

409.description: The path is not a file; or, comparing with the Working Tree, the Root is unavailable or its configuration has never been valid.

500.description: The history or the Working Tree could not be read.

get.summary: Whether a path is captured, and which rule at which level decided it.
get.description:
The answer is computed from the configuration and the Working Tree as they are now — the same
inputs the next capture reads — so it is the answer to "would the next Snapshot hold this file". An
excluded ancestor is named as such, because pruning wins over negation and a person reading only
the path's own rule would conclude the opposite (ADR 0007).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path, relative to the Root and `/`-separated. It need not exist.

200.description: Whether the path is captured, and why.

400.description: The path is malformed.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or its configuration cannot be read.

post.summary: Write a Snapshot's versions into a directory the request names, leaving the Working Tree untouched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: A dry run: what would happen to every file, and the selection's size; nothing written.

202.description: Planned, and queued as a job that plans again under the stores' locks and then writes each file to a temporary name beside it, renamed into place, with the Snapshot's permission bits — on Windows, none. Missing directories are made. A Withheld path is absent from the destination and its outcome says `skipped`, with its reason. Inside a Root, anything overwritten is first held by that Root's Safety Snapshot, named in the job's result.

400.description: `confirmation_required`: some file needs a confirmation (`overwrite`, `replace_type`, `dest_in_root`, `overwrite_unrecoverable`, or `"all"`) or a resolution (`write`, `rename_to`, `name_case`, `modes`), or cannot be written (`type_conflict`, `link_check_failed`); `paths` says what each needs and nothing was written. `dest_in_store`: the destination is inside a History Store. Otherwise a malformed path, destination or resolution.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path in the Snapshot.

409.description: `dest_unwritable`: the destination, or the nearest directory above it that is there, is not a directory. Otherwise the Root the destination lies inside is unavailable, or its configuration has never been valid.

500.description: The history could not be read.

post.summary: Remove every version of a path from the Root's whole history, as a job (ticket 81, ticket 06).
post.description:
Irreversible, so the request must say everything itself — what, that the caller knows, and whether
the path is excluded from now on; the daemon never asks (ticket 07). It ends with a Maintenance Pass
under the same lock, which is what takes the bytes off the disk, so it is refused while there is no
`git` to run it with. The Working Tree is never touched, and no Safety Snapshot is taken: one would
capture the very thing being removed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

202.description: Queued behind any capture of the Root in flight — or, asked for again while it still waits, that same job; `Location` and the body name it. Excluding from now on is in force from here.

400.description: Something the request must carry is missing (`confirmation_required`, `details.missing` naming it), or the glob is not one Forget can remove.

404.description: No such Root is watched, or kept since it was unwatched.

409.description: Excluding a path on the secret opt-in list, or no `git` to end with a Maintenance Pass.

delete.summary: Erase a Root's history and keep watching it: what `keepster purge` asks for (ticket 68).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

204.description: The Root's history is erased. A watched Root stays registered and watched, and its next capture starts the history over, reading every file again; one no longer watched is erased whole.

404.description: No such Root is watched, or kept since it was unwatched.

500.description: The history could not be erased.

post.summary:
Run a Maintenance Pass over the Root now, as a job: what is otherwise done daily, at a quiet moment,
on request — after a Retention that freed much, say.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

202.description: The pass is queued behind any capture of the Root in flight — or, asked for again while one still waits, that same job; `Location` and the body name it.

404.description: No such Root is watched, or kept since it was unwatched.

409.description: No `git` a pass can run with is usable, or the Root is unavailable.

get.summary:
List the Root's pinned Snapshots — including those of a Root no longer watched, whose last state
was pinned when it was unwatched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: The pinned Snapshots, newest first.

404.description: No such Root is watched, or kept since it was unwatched.

409.description: The Root is unavailable.

500.description: The history could not be read.

put.summary: Pin a Snapshot, so that it survives Retention unconditionally. Pinning a pinned one changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

404.description: No such Root or Snapshot.

409.description: The Root is unavailable.

500.description: The Pin could not be written.

delete.summary:
Unpin a Snapshot, which is Retention's again for as long as its Segment holds it. Unpinning one that
is not pinned changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

404.description: No such Root, or no such Snapshot identity.

409.description: The Root is unavailable.

500.description: The Pin could not be removed.

post.summary: Compare the Root's Working Tree against its latest Snapshot now, and capture what differs.
post.description:
The same pass the daemon runs at its start and after the platform loses events, run on request —
with `verify: hash`, reading every file. Nothing is written when nothing changed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: The pass ran; `snapshot` is the one it wrote, absent when nothing had changed.

400.description: The body is not JSON.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or its configuration has no valid version.

415.description: The body is not declared as `application/json`.

422.description: The body is JSON of the wrong shape, such as an unknown `verify`.

500.description: The Snapshot could not be written, or the clock cannot be recorded.

post.summary: Put a Snapshot's versions back over the Working Tree.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

200.description: Every file of the request, in path order, with what happened to it — or, for a dry run, what would — and the Safety Snapshot that undoes it. Restore overwrites and creates; it never deletes, so a file it created stays after an undo. Each file is written to a temporary name beside it and renamed into place, with the Snapshot's permission bits — or, where those on disk differ, the ones `modes` chose; a file whose content already matches has only its bits set. Windows keeps no permission bits, and sets none. A file that changed between the plan and its write fails without being touched.

400.description: `confirmation_required`: some file needs a confirmation (`create_parents`, `replace_type`, `break_hardlinks`, `overwrite_unrecoverable`, or `"all"` for every one) or a resolution (`write`, `rename_to`, `name_case`, `modes`, which the blanket force never gives — `modes` defaults to the Root's `restore.modes` setting, which by default asks), or cannot be restored (`type_conflict`, `link_check_failed`). Nothing was written and no Safety Snapshot taken; `paths` says what each file needs. Otherwise a malformed path or resolution.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path in the Snapshot — or a path asked for by name is Withheld there (`withheld`), so there is nothing to restore.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or its configuration has never been valid.

415.description: The body is not declared as `application/json`.

422.description: The body is JSON of the wrong shape.

500.description: The history could not be read, or the Safety Snapshot could not be taken — in which case nothing was written.

get.summary: One page of a Root's chronology, newest first — or, with `path`, of the Snapshots that changed it.
get.description:
One endpoint for both questions, because they return the same shape and a client would otherwise
render one table with two code paths (ticket 07). A Root never captured has an empty chronology.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only the Snapshots that changed this Root-relative path.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only Snapshots taken at or before this RFC 3339 moment.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only Snapshots taken strictly after this RFC 3339 moment.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many; 100 by default, 1000 at most.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

200.description: One page of the chronology, newest first. A Root never captured has an empty one.

400.description: A parameter is malformed.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The Root is unavailable.

500.description: The history could not be read.

post.summary: Capture the Root's current contents now.
post.description:
Ticket 43 adds the Triggers that make this happen by itself; until then a capture is something a
person or a script asks for, which is also what lets the write path be exercised end to end.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
The Root's identity, in its canonical form. A prefix or a path names no Root here: resolving
those is the client's convenience, done before the request.

201.description: The Snapshot just taken. It may be incomplete: some files could not be read, and `omitted` names them.

404.description: No such Root is registered.

409.description: The Root is unavailable: its directory or its record is missing or unreadable — or its configuration cannot be read, which refuses the capture rather than dropping the user's rules.

500.description: The Snapshot could not be written, or the clock cannot be recorded.

get.summary:
A selection of a Snapshot as one zip archive, for a client that cannot be given a destination — the
browser's download.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A file or a directory, Root-relative; the whole Snapshot when absent.

200.description: A zip64 archive, streamed, every file stored uncompressed with its permission bits, so its size is known first: `Content-Length` is what `stat` said. A Withheld path is absent, as from any export; `stat` names them. Generated as it is sent, so it cannot be resumed — an interrupted download starts again.

400.description: The path is malformed.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path.

500.description: The history could not be read.

get.summary: One version's raw bytes, with `Content-Length`, `ETag` and `Range` (ticket 07).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file, Root-relative.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description:
`1` (or `true`) to have a browser save it rather than show it: `Content-Disposition: attachment`,
named as the file is — the whole of downloading one file (ticket 58).

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One byte range, as `bytes=first-last`, `bytes=first-` or `bytes=-suffix`. Several ranges, or one that cannot be parsed, are answered with the whole content.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: An `ETag` this API returned for the same version; a match is answered with `304`.

200.description: The version's raw bytes, streamed.

Content-Disposition.description: With `download=1`: `attachment`, named as the file is.

Content-Length.description: The size of the version in bytes.

ETag.description: Names the content: equal tags mean equal bytes.

206.description: The requested range of the version's bytes.

ETag.description: Names the whole content, not the range.

304.description: The client's copy, named by `If-None-Match`, is current.

400.description: A parameter is malformed.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path — or the path is Withheld in the Snapshot (`withheld`), which holds no content for it.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or the path is not a file.

416.description: The range lies outside the content. No body.

500.description: The history could not be read.

get.summary: The paths a Snapshot holds under a directory.
get.description:
Shallow by default, because a 50 000-file tree is expanded lazily in a UI anyway; `infinity` serves
the CLI and scripts (ticket 07).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory to list, Root-relative; the Root itself when absent.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: `1` for the directory's own children (the default), `infinity` for everything beneath it.

200.description: The paths the Snapshot holds under the directory, in byte order — with those it names without holding them: Withheld, or omitted from an incomplete Snapshot.

400.description: A parameter is malformed.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path.

409.description: The Root is unavailable, or the path is not a directory.

500.description: The history could not be read.

get.summary: How much a selection of a Snapshot holds, so its size is shown before an Export or a download.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Root's identity, in its canonical form.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description: The Snapshot's identity, as the timeline returned it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A file or a directory, Root-relative; the whole Snapshot when absent.

200.description: Its files and bytes, the exact size of its archive, and what it withholds.

400.description: The path is malformed.

404.description: No such Root, Snapshot or path.

500.description: The history could not be read.

get.summary: Find text in every version a Root's history holds, streamed as it is found.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to find in the content: a literal, matched case-insensitively unless it has a capital.

parameters.name: regex
parameters.description: `true` to read `q` as a regular expression, matched in linear time.

parameters.name: roots
parameters.description:
The Roots to search, by identity, comma-separated. One is the usual: a content search reads every
version stored, so asking for every Root is said with `all`.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: `true` to search every Root — those no longer watched whose history is kept included.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A file or directory, Root-relative: only what is at or beneath it is read.

200.description: An `application/x-ndjson` stream: a `plan` record first, saying how many distinct versions and bytes each Root will have read; then `match` records — one per content version, a path and the range of Snapshots its content was current for, never one per Snapshot — and `withheld` records for paths with no content to search, with `progress` now and then; and a `summary` last, counting versions scanned, binaries skipped and Withheld paths met. A version is read once however many Snapshots held it; a binary one is skipped and counted; the metadata sidecar is never searched. Outside the read budget: no time is promised, and closing the connection stops the walk.

400.description: `q` is missing or empty, or not a regular expression that compiles, or the query string cannot be read (`query_invalid`); no Root named and `all` not asked (`search_invalid`); or `path` is malformed.

404.description: A Root asked for is not known.

500.description: The Registry could not be read, so which Roots there are is unknown (`registry_failed`).

get.summary: Find a path by its name in the history of every Root, a file long deleted included.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A fragment of the path, matched anywhere in it — case-insensitively unless it has a capital.

parameters.name: glob
parameters.description: `true` to read `q` as an Include Rules pattern, as the configuration writes them: `**/*.env`.

parameters.name: roots
parameters.description:
The Roots to search, by identity, comma-separated; every Root when absent — those no longer
watched whose history is kept included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many paths to answer with: 100 unless given, and at most 1000.

200.description: Every path any Snapshot changed that the query finds, by Root and then by path: how many Snapshots changed it, the first and the last, and whether the newest Snapshot still holds it. Answered from the index, inside the chronology budget.

400.description: `q` is missing or empty, or not a pattern, or the query string cannot be read (`query_invalid`); `limit` is not a positive whole number (`limit_invalid`).

404.description: A Root asked for is not known.

500.description: The Registry could not be read, so which Roots there are is unknown (`registry_failed`).

get.summary: The whole health surface.

200.description: The daemon and every Watched Root. `keepster status --json` prints exactly this.

500.description: The Registry could not be read.

put.summary: Report what a tray can do, renewing its report.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: The name the tray reports under, the same for as long as it runs: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`.

204.description: Recorded: `status` lists it under `trays` for 90 seconds, so a tray renews it every 30, and a tray that died drops out by itself.

400.description: An instance that is not a plain name (`tray_invalid`), or a body that is not this JSON (`body_invalid`).

delete.summary: A tray is leaving: withdraw its report.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: The name the tray reported under.

204.description: Withdrawn. Withdrawing a report never made, or one already expired, is no error.

400.description: An instance that is not a plain name (`tray_invalid`).

post.summary: A single-use code for opening a browser session, inside the URL to open.

200.description: The URL to open. Its code is exchanged once, for an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie, and redirected away from. Served on the control channel alone.

409.description: The daemon has no loopback listener: `ui.listener` is off, or it could not bind (`listener_unavailable`).

500.description: No code could be minted.

post.summary: Replace the token, revoking every browser session and every code not yet exchanged.

204.description: A new token is in force and in its file; every session the old one opened is refused from now on. A restart rotates it too. Served on the control channel alone.

409.description: The daemon has no loopback listener, so there is no token (`listener_unavailable`).

500.description: The new token could not be written; the old one stays in force.

get.summary:
Every Root no longer watched whose history is kept (ticket 68): the identities that reach those
histories, which `GET /v1/roots` does not list.

200.description: Every Root no longer watched whose history is kept; empty when there is none.

500.description: The Registry could not be read.

get.summary: Which build and which API this daemon is.

200.description: The build and the API it speaks. Served before authentication.

Alarm.description:
Something that stopped the insurance, as the daemon decides it (ticket 67): a client delivers it
and decides nothing (ADR 0008).

One alarm per Root for its state, which a change of state replaces and a return to `watching`
clears, and one per kind of job on a Root, which the next job of that kind that succeeds clears.

job.description: The job that failed, for `job_failed`: `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` says what went wrong.

job_kind.description: What that job did, for `job_failed`: `maintenance`, `forget` or `export`.

kind.description:
What is wrong: `root_unavailable`, `root_degraded` or `job_failed`. An open set, as error codes
are: a client shows an alarm of a kind it does not know by its Root.

reason.description: The Root's `state_code`, for an alarm about its state.

Change.description: How one path differs between a Snapshot and the Snapshot before it.

ConfigEntry.description: One entry of a layered list, and where it was written.

ConfigKey.description: One key of a Root's effective configuration.

entries.description:
For a pattern list, every entry and where it was written, from the least specific level to the
most — which is the order the last matching pattern is found in.

key.description: The key as a person writes it, `table.key`.

origin.description:
Where the value was set: the most specific level that set a scalar — the built-in default when
none did — and, for a list, its last entry's.

restart_required.description:
Whether a file sets this key to something else that only a restart applies. The value above is
the one in force.

value.description:
The value in force, typed as the key is: a switch, a number of bytes, a duration written as text
in the largest whole unit (`3s`, `1m`, `1h`), or a list. A pattern list holds its patterns as
written; `files.max_size_by_pattern` holds `{ pattern, max }` objects; `triggers.active` holds the
names of the active Triggers.

ConfigLevel.description:
The levels configuration is layered in, from the least specific to the most — the provenance enum
of ticket 04, plus the watched directory's own ignore files, which sit beneath everything the user
writes.

ConfigWarning.description: Something about the configuration that is defined but almost certainly not what was meant.

code.description: What kind of warning: `negation_unreachable` or `key_ignored`. An open set.

message.description: What it means here, for a person.

oneOf.description: `"all"`: every confirmation.
These.

Confirm.description: The confirmations a Restore request gives.

Confirmation.description: A structural change a Restore must be told it may make.

oneOf.description:
What the search will read, before it reads any of it: per Root, its distinct versions and their
size. No time is promised: the cost is stored content, not a number of Snapshots.
A line of a version that matched.

content.description: The version's content identity, opaque: equal for equal content, wherever it is.

first.description: The first Snapshot that held this content at this path.

oneOf.description: A path the walk met with no content to search: it was Withheld.

kind.description: For a special file, what kind.

reason.description: Why: `too_large`, `special_file`, and the rest of the Withheld reasons.

snapshot.description: The first Snapshot it was Withheld in.

oneOf.description: How far the walk has got in one Root.
A Root the walk could not search, and why; the others go on.
What the whole walk looked at: sent last, so that finding nothing is told apart from not looking.

binaries_skipped.description: Versions skipped as binary: a NUL among their first bytes.

unreadable.description: Versions the store could not read.

withheld.description: Withheld paths met, each named in a `withheld` record.

ContentRecord.description:
One line of a content search, as `GET /v1/search/content` streams them (ticket 59): the cost first,
then every match and every Withheld path as the walk meets them, progress now and then, and a summary
last. A record of a type a client does not know is to be passed over.

The walk reads each distinct version once, however many Snapshots held it, so a match is a **content
version** — a path, and the range of Snapshots its content was current for — never one row per
Snapshot.

allOf.description: Which build, which API and which store format: the fields the version handshake returns.

alarms.description:
The alarms in force: what stopped the insurance, as the last `alarms.changed` announced it
(ticket 67). A client that connects after an incident learns it here, because a replayed stream
is not a snapshot of state. Empty while nothing is wrong; absent from a daemon older than the
field.

autostart.description: Whether the daemon comes back at login: its autostart unit is installed and enabled (ticket 61).

autostart_reason.description:
Why autostart is unavailable: `not_installed` — a state of its own, never read as stopped — or
`disabled`. An open set, as error codes are.

git.description: The external `git` maintenance runs with, or why there is none.

linger.description: Whether coverage survives the user's logout (ticket 61).

linger_reason.description:
Why it does not: `logout_gap` where the platform ends a user's agents at logout (macOS,
Windows), or `disabled` where linger could be switched on and is not (Linux). An open set.

oneOf.description:
Whether the daemon has a network surface: the loopback listener the browser reaches it through
(ticket 60). The only place that says so. Switched off, it is a deliberate configuration rather
than a fault, and changes no exit code. Absent from a daemon older than the field.

The daemon's log: the level it writes at, and a raise while one lasts (ticket 62). Absent from a
daemon older than the field.

maintenance.description:
Whether store maintenance can run at all, which depends on the external `git` (ticket 52). While
it cannot, nothing Retention removes is reclaimed, and `keepster status` exits non-zero.

muted_until.description:
Until when notifications are muted, as an RFC 3339 moment. Present only while a mute lasts, so a
mute is never a silent failure; alarms are still raised and listed while it does, and it changes
no exit code.

pid.description:
The daemon's process id, informational only — the pid file's lock, not its content, is the
single-instance authority (ticket 05).

trays.description:
The trays attached, each with its two capability rows as it last reported them (ticket 67).
Empty when no tray is attached; absent from a daemon older than the field. Changes no exit code.

uptime_seconds.description: How long this daemon has been serving, measured monotonically.

Decision.description: What a capture does with one path.

DiagnosticConfiguration.description: The effective configuration: the global level on its own, and every Root's.

global.description:
The defaults and the global file's own table — what every Root starts from, and what the keys
describing the daemon are set by.

roots.description: Every watched Root's effective configuration, in registration order.

Diagnostics.description:
What the daemon knows that a diagnostics bundle carries, as `GET /v1/diagnostics` serves it on the
control channel alone (ticket 63).

The bundle discloses by inventory and never redacts (ADR 0013): paths are here as they are, because
the defects this exists for cannot be diagnosed without them. What is never here is a byte of any
file from history — every section is read from status, configuration, the Registry, refs, commit
messages and the index, and none from a blob. Each section carries its own failure, so one that
cannot be read leaves the others whole.

configuration.description: The effective configuration with the level that set each key.

environment.description: What the daemon runs on and with.

log.description: The tail of the daemon's log, and the format it is written in.

registry.description: Every Root the Registry holds, watched or not, with its record as written.

status.description: The health surface, exactly as `GET /v1/status` serves it.

topology.description: What each Root's store holds, one entry per Root the Registry holds.

oneOf.description:
The tail of the tray's log, read beside the daemon's (ticket 67); absent when the daemon writes
no log file and so knows no directory to read it from.

watermarks.description: How far each Root's derived index got, one entry per Root the Registry holds.

Diff.description:
What changed from a Snapshot to another Snapshot or the Working Tree — the answer of
`GET /v1/roots/{id}/diff` (ticket 46).

Computed by the daemon, which holds both sides, so binary detection, rename detection and the size
past which no hunks are computed are decided once and every client shows the same lines.

files.description:
Without `path`, every changed file in path order and without hunks; with it, that one file with
its hunks.

from.description: The older side: a Snapshot's identity.

omitted.description:
Working Tree files that could not be read. Each keeps its last captured content, as a capture
keeps it, so the comparison is not whole there.

to.description:
The newer side: a Snapshot's identity, or `working` for the Working Tree as the next Snapshot
would hold it.

DiffFile.description: One file's part of a diff.

binary.description: Whether either version is binary, by git's rule: no hunks are computed for it.

oneOf.description: How it changed; absent for a path asked about that did not change.

hunks.description: The changed lines with their context. Empty in a summary, and for a binary or too large file.

new_mode.description: The file's mode on the newer side, when it differs from `old_mode`.

old_mode.description:
The file's permission bits on the older side, all twelve as `entries` gives them in
`permissions` — present, with `new_mode`, when they changed, alone or with the content.

old_path.description: Where a renamed file was on the older side.

path.description:
Where the file is on the newer side — or, for a deletion, where it was. Relative to the Root. A
directory is named only when its permission bits are all that changed there.

too_large.description:
Whether either version is larger than the daemon diffs, 8 MiB: no hunks are computed for it, and
it is not probed for being binary.

withheld.description:
Why the next Snapshot would not hold a file that is still in the Working Tree — `too_large` in
this version — which is why it reads as deleted, and is not.

DiffHunk.description: One run of changed lines with the context around it.

new_lines.description: How many lines of the newer side it covers.

new_start.description: The run's first line on the newer side, counting from 1.

old_lines.description: How many lines of the older side it covers.

old_start.description: The run's first line on the older side, counting from 1.

newline.description: `false` for a file's last line when the file ends without a newline; absent otherwise.

text.description:
The line without its ending. Text that is not UTF-8 is shown with replacement characters; the
unified format carries the exact bytes.

DirectoryListing.description: The directories in one directory on the daemon's machine, for choosing where an Export writes.

directories.description: Every directory in it, by name; no file, no link, no size.

parent.description: The directory above it, absent at the top.

Entries.description: The paths a Snapshot holds under a directory, as `…/entries` serves them.

entries.description: One per path, in byte order of the path.

unrecognized.description:
Records of the Snapshot's own metadata this build does not know, as they are written — skipped,
and reported, because a later build recorded facts this one cannot show. Absent when there are
none.

binary.description:
Whether the content is binary by git's rule. A display flag only: binary files are stored as
they are (ticket 10). Absent for anything but a file, and for a packed file over a megabyte,
which would have to be read whole to tell (ticket 52).

incomplete.description:
Why it is not held as it was when the Snapshot was taken, which makes the Snapshot incomplete:
`unstable` (it kept changing while read) or the read error's symbolic name — `eacces` on Unix,
`sharing_violation` on Windows. With `omitted` nothing is held; on a file, its previous version
was kept. An open set.

mode.description:
A file's tree mode as permission bits, `420` (`0o644`) or `493` (`0o755`): whether it is
executable, on every platform. Absent for anything but a file.

path.description: Where it is, relative to the Root, `/`-separated.

permissions.description:
All twelve permission bits of a file or directory as the Snapshot holds them, as a number
(`384` is `0o600`). Absent where the capture observed none — on Windows, or before ticket 50 —
and for anything else.

size.description: Its size in bytes. Absent for a directory.

oneOf.description: With `withheld`: why the Snapshot holds no content for it.

EntryKind.description: What kind of thing a Snapshot holds at a path.

Environment.description: What the daemon runs on, and with.

arch.description: The processor architecture, as Rust names it: `x86_64`, `aarch64`.

filesystems.description: The filesystem under each Root whose record can be read, in registration order.

git.description: The external `git` maintenance runs with, or why there is none: the discovery result.

maintenance.description:
How each Root's last Maintenance Pass since the daemon started ended, in registration order. A
Root with no pass since then has no entry: the record is kept in memory, not on disk.

os.description: The operating system, as Rust names it: `linux`, `macos`, `windows`.

watches.description: The directory watches every Root holds together, against the daemon-wide ceiling.

oneOf.description: A Snapshot was written, by whichever Trigger.

changed_paths.description:
How many paths differ from the Snapshot before it; absent when the count failed after the
Snapshot was written.

incomplete.description: Whether some file meant to be captured could not be read.

oneOf.description: A directory became a Watched Root.
A Root was deregistered.

purged.description: Whether its History Store was erased with it.

root.description: The Root that is no longer watched.

oneOf.description:
A Root's history was erased on request (ticket 68). A client showing its timeline refetches it:
every Snapshot it shows is gone. A Root still watched stays watched and captures afresh.
A Root's directory was recorded at a new path.
What the daemon can promise for a Root changed.

state_code.description: The reason behind a state that is not `watching`, as `GET /v1/roots/{id}` gives it.

oneOf.description:
A Root's configuration in force changed: a file was edited and every file it depends on is
valid.

A file a Root's configuration depends on became invalid, so the last known-good version stays
in force for it — or, without one, the Root is not captured.

root.description: The Root the invalid file affects.

oneOf.description: A Restore wrote what it was asked to, as far as it could.

failed.description: How many could not be written.

safety_snapshot.description: Its Safety Snapshot, which undoes it.

oneOf.description:
A Retention pass removed Snapshots the ladder no longer keeps (ticket 51). Sent only when it
removed something; a client showing the timeline refetches it.

deleted_segments.description: How many Segments were deleted whole.

thinned_segments.description: How many were re-chained with fewer Snapshots.

oneOf.description: A Maintenance Pass reclaimed what nothing references any more and packed the rest (ticket 52).
A job left the queue and is under way (ticket 54).

kind.description: What it does: `maintenance`. The set grows inside `/v1`.

oneOf.description: A job got further: `done` of `total` steps, in units of its own.
A job ended; `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` has its result or what went wrong.

The alarms in force changed, or the mute did (ticket 67). Changes are gathered for five seconds
and sent together; an alarm raised and cleared inside those seconds is never sent.

alarms.description: Every alarm in force now, as `status` lists them.

cleared.description: The alarms no longer in force.

muted_until.description:
Until when notifications are muted, while they are; a mute changed alone sends this event
with nothing raised or cleared.

raised.description:
The alarms raised since the last `alarms.changed`. One that replaces another for the same
Root is here, with the one it replaces in `cleared`.

oneOf.description:
The daemon is stopping on purpose, and the stream ends after this. A stream that ends without
it is a daemon that died.
The level the daemon's log is written at changed: a raise began or ended (ticket 67).

until.description: When a raise ends, as an RFC 3339 moment, while one lasts.

oneOf.description:
The events since the client's `Last-Event-ID` cannot be replayed: they were evicted, the daemon
restarted, or the client fell too far behind. Whatever it shows may be stale, so it refetches.

Event.description:
One event on the live stream, `GET /v1/events` (ticket 45).

Payloads are thin on purpose — identities and flags, never content: a client wanting detail fetches it
through the endpoint that already serves that shape, so no second rendering of a Root or a Snapshot
exists to drift. The set grows inside `/v1` as behaviour is added (retention, maintenance, jobs), so a
client must pass over an event whose name it does not know.

Explanation.description:
Whether one path is captured, and which rule decided it — the answer of `GET …/explain`.

The analogue of `git check-ignore -v`, and the answer to "why wasn't my file saved": it names the
rule a person wrote, at which level and on which line, rather than describing a computation.

captured.description: Whether a Snapshot taken now would hold its content.

decision.description: What a capture does with it.

max_size.description: The size cap that applies to it, in bytes.

max_size_origin.description:
Where the scalar cap was set — the built-in default, or a configuration file's `max_size`. A
per-pattern cap that applies instead is named in `rule`.

oneOf.description:
What is at the path in the Working Tree right now; absent when nothing is. A path need not exist
to be explained, and one that does not is explained as a file.

The last of the user's rules matching the path itself, reported even when an ancestor prunes it
or the denylist refuses it — so the answer can say what that rule would have done.

path.description: The path asked about, relative to the Root.

pruned_by.description: With `pruned`, the excluded ancestor directory that is never entered.

reason.description:
With `withheld`, why: `too_large`, `reserved_name` (the directory's own `.git`), `special_file`
(a FIFO, socket or device), `history_store` or `other_root`. An open set, as `Withheld::reason`
is.

oneOf.description:
The rule behind the decision: the exclude rule, the pruning ancestor's exclude rule, the
denylist entry, the per-pattern cap — or, for a captured path, the include or opt-in that let it
in. Absent when no rule was involved.

size.description: Its size, when it is a file on disk.

warnings.description:
What the configuration defines but almost certainly does not mean — a negation an excluded
ancestor makes unreachable, a key a Root's own file may not set. None of them makes the Root
`Degraded`.

ExportPlan.description: What an Export would do, as a dry run answers it.

dest.description: The directory it would write into.

files.description: How many files the selection holds, Withheld paths aside.

paths.description: Every file of the request, in path order, with what would happen to it.

ExportRequest.description:
An Export, as `POST /v1/roots/{id}/export` takes it (ticket 58): a Snapshot's versions written into a
directory the request names, the Working Tree untouched.

Restore's request, less what only a Restore needs, and with a destination: the whole request is
checked before anything is written, and a path that needs a confirmation or a resolution stops it.

confirm.description:
The changes agreed to: `overwrite`, `replace_type`, `dest_in_root`, `overwrite_unrecoverable`, or
`"all"` for every one — which settles no resolution.

dest.description:
The directory written into, absolute, on the daemon's machine — which is the client's, since the
daemon listens only there. Each file goes at its Snapshot path beneath it; it is made if missing.

dry_run.description:
Plan only: answer with what would happen to every path and the selection's size, and write
nothing.

from.description: The Snapshot whose versions are written, by identity.

oneOf.description:
Where a file already at the destination has other permission bits than the Snapshot's
(`modes_differ`) and no answer of its own: take the Snapshot's, or keep those there.

paths.description: Root-relative paths; a directory means everything beneath it, and none means the whole Snapshot.

resolutions.description: Answers to what only the user can settle, keyed by the Snapshot path they are for.

skip_unresolvable.description: Skip each path still in the way, with its reasons, rather than stop the request.

FileChange.description: How a file changed between the two sides of a diff.

FollowTargets.description: How the targets of a Root's followed links are covered.

count.description: How many links the last pass followed.

interval.description: How often they are passed over, in seconds.

last_reconciled_at.description: When a pass last covered them, in UTC, as RFC 3339; absent before the first.

ForgetRequest.description:
A Forget, as `POST /v1/roots/{id}/forget` takes it. Every field must be there: the daemon never asks,
it refuses with `confirmation_required`, and the asking is the CLI's (ticket 07).

confirm.description: `true`: this is irreversible, and the caller knows it.

glob.description: What to remove from every Snapshot, as an Include Rule pattern relative to the Root.

on_exclude.description:
`exclude` keeps the pattern out of history from now on; `keep-watching` goes on capturing it —
right for a file that only held a secret for a while, wrong for one that still does.

GitStatus.description: The external `git` store maintenance runs with (ticket 52). Capture never needs it.

detail.description: What running it said, for `not_executable` and `failed`: its error, word for word.

oneOf.description: How to install one, while maintenance cannot run. Keepster never runs it itself.

minimum.description: The oldest version maintenance runs with.

path.description: Where it is: found in configuration (`git.path`) or a stable place — never an inherited `PATH`.

reason.description:
Why maintenance cannot run: `missing`, `macos_stub`, `not_executable`, `too_old` or `failed`. An
open set, as error codes are.

GlobalConfiguration.description: The global level of the configuration.

errors.description:
The global file, when its current version is invalid and not applied, in the standard error
shape.

file.description: The global file, where there is one.

keys.description:
Every key of the schema, with its value and the level that set it, in the order the schema
lists them. Empty while the global file has never had a valid version.

command.description: The command for this platform's package manager, when it is recognised.

Job.description:
A long or irreversible operation, as `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` reports it (ticket 54, ticket 07). Jobs live
in the daemon's memory: a restart forgets them.

oneOf.description: Why it failed, in the shape of every other failure.

kind.description:
What it does: `maintenance`. The set grows inside `/v1`, so a client must accept a kind it does
not know.

oneOf.description: How far it got, for a job that counts its steps.
What it did, once it succeeded.

state.description: Where it is in its life.

JobAccepted.description: A job just accepted, as `202` answers it; `Location` names the same job.

job_id.description: The job's identity, by which `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` reports it.

JobProgress.description: How far a job got: `done` of `total` steps, in units of its own.

JobResult.description:
What a job did. Each kind fills in what it measures, so every field is optional and more arrive
inside `/v1` as kinds are added.

blobs_removed.description: Forget: how many contents no Snapshot holds any more.

excluded.description: Forget: whether what it removed is kept out of history from now on.

left_alone.description:
Forget: refs among the Segments' and Pins' names this build could not read, and so left as they
are — naming no commit, or written by a newer Keepster in a content format this build does not
know — named because what they hold was not forgotten, and nothing is passed over in silence.

paths.description:
Export: every file of the request, in path order, with what happened to it — `restored` meaning
written over what was there.

reclaimed_bytes.description: A Maintenance Pass — and the one Forget ends with: how much smaller the store is on disk.

removed_paths.description: Forget: every Root-relative path it removed.

safety_snapshot.description:
Export into a Root, overwriting something there: the Snapshot of that Root taken just before,
which what was overwritten can be restored from.

snapshots_touched.description: Forget: how many Snapshots held a matching path, and hold none now.

still_on_disk.description:
Forget: the removed paths whose file in the Working Tree still holds what was removed. Forget
never touches the Working Tree, so the secret there still needs rotating — and, unless `excluded`,
the next Snapshot captures it again.

JobState.description: Where a job is in its life: queued, then running, then succeeded or failed — once, in that order.

LineKind.description: Which side of a diff a line is on.

ListenerState.description: Whether the loopback listener exists. Decided when the daemon starts, and only a restart changes it.

ListenerStatus.description: The loopback listener: where it is, or why there is none.

address.description: Where it listens, `127.0.0.1:<port>`, while it does.

detail.description: Why it could not bind, while it `failed`.

LogFileTail.description: The end of one log file.

name.description: The file's name in the log directory: `daemon.log`, `daemon.log.1`, …

size.description: The file's whole size, in bytes.

text.description: Its last lines, whole lines only.

truncated.description: Whether the lines before these were left out.

LogLevelRequest.description: A raise of the log level, which always ends: `PUT /v1/log/level`.

for.description:
How long, as a duration such as `30m` or `2h`: at least a second, at most seven days. Required:
a level left raised by forgetting is not a state this API can reach.

level.description: The level to write at: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`.

LogStatus.description: The daemon's log, as `status` shows it.

default.description: The level configured by `log.level`, which a raise returns to by itself.

file.description: The file the log is written to, when the daemon writes one.

level.description: The level written at now: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`.

until.description:
When a raised level ends, as an RFC 3339 moment. Present only while a raise lasts: a state that
changes what the daemon does is never silent.

LogTail.description: The tail of a log: the daemon's, or the tray's.

error.description: Why the log could not be read, when it could not.

files.description:
The current file and then each rotated one, newest first, until the tail's budget is spent.
Empty when the daemon writes no log file, or when its log could not be read.

format.description:
The format its lines are written in, `text` or `json`: the daemon's as `log.format` set it at the
start, where a rotated file written before a restart may be in the other; the tray's always
`text`.

MaintenancePass.description: How one Root's last Maintenance Pass ended.

error.description: Why the pass did not run, when it did not.

finished_at.description: When it ended, as an RFC 3339 moment.

outcome.description:
How: `succeeded`; `failed`, when `git` ran and failed it; `git_unavailable`, when the `git` failed
its check before the pass; `history_unreadable`, when the store could not be opened so `git`
never ran. An open set, as error codes are.

reclaimed_bytes.description: What a pass that succeeded reclaimed, in bytes.

stderr.description:
What `git` wrote to its error stream, word for word, when it failed. A pass that succeeded keeps
none: `git` runs quietly, and its error stream is kept only when it fails.

ModesChoice.description: Which permission bits a restored file ends up with, where the Snapshot's and the disk's differ.

MuteRequest.description: A mute of the notifications, which always ends: `PUT /v1/alarms/mute`.

minutes.description: How long, in minutes: 1 to 1440. Absent, an hour.

MuteStatus.description: Whether notifications are muted, as `PUT` and `DELETE /v1/alarms/mute` answer.

until.description: Until when, as an RFC 3339 moment; absent while nothing is muted.

NameCaseChoice.description: Which name a file restored over a name in another case keeps.

OnDiskKind.description: What is at a path in the Working Tree.

Origin.description: Where a rule or a value was set.

level.description: The level it was set at.

line.description: Its line in that file, where it has one.

source.description: The file it was written in, or a description of a built-in value.

PathHit.description: One path a path search found.

exists.description:
Whether the newest Snapshot still holds it: `false` is a file already gone, which only its
history still has.

root.description: The Root it is in, by identity.

PathResolution.description: The answer to one path's question; exactly one field is set.

oneOf.description: For `modes_differ`: take the Snapshot's permission bits, or keep those on disk.
For `name_case`: keep the name already on disk, or take the Snapshot's.

rename_to.description: For `name_invalid`: write the file under this bare name in the same directory.

write.description: For `name_collision`: write this path, and skip the others that are one file with it.

PathSearch.description:
What a path search found, as `GET /v1/search/paths` answers it (ticket 59): every path any Snapshot
changed whose name the query finds, in every Root asked — a file long gone from the Working Tree
included, which nothing else in the product can reach.

hits.description: Every path found, by Root and then by path.

truncated.description: Whether there were more than `limit`; ask for fewer paths with a narrower query.

unsearched.description: Roots whose history could not be read, and so were not searched.

format.description: The content format of the Snapshot it holds; absent when it names none this build knows of.

snapshot.description: The pinned Snapshot's identity, which is the ref's name.

Pins.description: A Root's pinned Snapshots, as `GET /v1/roots/{id}/pins` serves them: few enough to need no page.

unreadable.description:
The Pins, as `pins/` and the Snapshot's identity, written by a newer Keepster in a format this
build cannot read: pinned still, and not listed above. Absent while there are none.

Preferences.description:
The web UI's preferences: what `GET /v1/preferences` answers and `PUT /v1/preferences` replaces
whole (ticket 66, ticket 16).

Every key is required in a `PUT` today. A key added inside `/v1` will be optional there, an absent
one keeping the value stored, so a client older than the key cannot erase it.

syntax_line_limit.description: The longest line, in characters, a diff is still syntax-highlighted with: 1 to 10 000 000.

theme.description:
The palette: `system`, which follows the operating system's light or dark setting, `light` or
`dark`. A string rather than an enum, so that a palette added inside `/v1` is not a breaking
change to a client that reads this.

wrap_lines.description: Whether the diff wraps long lines rather than scrolling sideways.

PreviewConfig.description: A directory's own `.keepster.toml`, as a preview shows it.

sets.description: Every key it sets, in schema order, with what it sets it to.

warnings.description: What it defines that is almost certainly not meant.

PreviewGroup.description: Everything one rule — or one reason, or no rule at all — decided.

pruned.description: The directories it pruned, named and unmeasured.

oneOf.description: The rule, absent where none decided.
What is previewed, sent before the walk starts.

The directory's own `.keepster.toml`, when it has one: honoured exactly as registering it would
honour it, and shown, so that a rule a repository's author wrote is not read as Keepster's.

overlaps.description: A Root it contains, when it is none: registering it would be refused.

root.description: The Root it is, or lies inside, when there is one.

within.description:
Where it lies inside that Root, `/`-separated, when it is not the Root itself: classified by the
Root's rules, as a capture of the Root would classify it.

oneOf.description: One path, as the walk classified it.

bytes.description: Its apparent size in bytes: a file's length, a link's target text; nothing for a directory.

path.description: Where, relative to the directory previewed.

pruned.description: Whether it is an excluded directory the walk did not enter, as a capture never would.

reason.description: Why it is Withheld, for a Withheld path.

oneOf.description: The rule that decided, where one did.

How many paths the walk has classified so far, sent now and then whether or not any is listed —
so a reader sees the walk is alive, and the walk sees a reader that went away.
Why the walk stopped short, sent instead of the summary.
What the whole walk found.

excluded.description: What the rules and the secret denylist leave out.

groups.description: Every rule that decided something, and what it decided, largest first.

largest_captured.description: The largest files captured, largest first.

largest_left_out.description:
The largest files left out, largest first: excluded ones that were measured, and those
withheld without their content.

past_ceiling.description:
Which of v1's claims for one Root it is past: `files`, `directories`, `bytes`. Nothing is
refused above them; registering asks for a confirmation.

unreadable.description: How many paths could not be looked at.

withheld.description: What would be recorded without its content, by reason.

PreviewRecord.description:
One line of a Capture Preview, as `GET /v1/preview` streams them: a `header` first, then an `entry`
for every path asked for as the walk classifies it, interleaved with `progress`, then a `summary` — or,
if the walk fails, an `error` in its place. One JSON object per line (ticket 57); a record of a type a
client does not know is to be passed over.

A preview captures nothing and says nothing of what the History Store would grow by: that is
unknowable without hashing every file, which is the capture. What it measures is content to capture.

PreviewSetting.description: One key a directory's own `.keepster.toml` sets.

key.description: The key as a person writes it, `table.key`.

values.description:
What the file writes for it, typed as `ConfigKey::value` types a value: one for a scalar, every
entry the file adds for a list.

PreviewSize.description: One path and its apparent size.

path.description: Where, relative to the directory previewed.

PreviewTotals.description: How many files and directories, and how many bytes of files.

pruned.description: Excluded directories not entered, and so not measured.

Problem.description:
A failure, in the one shape every endpoint uses.

RFC 9457 Problem Details plus a `code` extension: a standard shape is what a third-party client's
library already parses, and `code` — not the prose of `title` or `detail` — is the stable part
clients branch on. The code set is deliberately **open** (ADR 0005): a client must treat a code it
does not know as its HTTP status.

code.description:
The stable, machine-readable code of the problem. Contract, unlike the prose of `title` and `detail`.

The set is open: it may grow inside `/v1`, so a client must treat an unknown code as the problem's HTTP status. The codes this version knows:

- `root_not_found`: No Root with this identity is registered.
- `snapshot_not_found`: No Snapshot with this identity is in the Root's history.
- `path_not_found`: The Snapshot holds nothing at this path.
- `root_overlaps`: The directory is inside, or contains, a Root that is already registered.
- `root_unavailable`: The Root cannot be served: its directory or its record is missing or unreadable.
- `not_a_file`: The path names something other than a file, so it has no content to read.
- `not_a_directory`: The path names something other than a directory, so it has no entries to list.
- `path_invalid`: A path is malformed: not absolute where it must be, or not Root-relative where it must be.
- `limit_invalid`: `limit` is not a positive whole number.
- `cursor_invalid`: `cursor` is not a `next_cursor` this API returned.
- `moment_invalid`: A moment is not an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `depth_invalid`: `depth` is neither `1` nor `infinity`.
- `registry_failed`: The Registry of Watched Roots could not be read or written.
- `capture_failed`: A Snapshot could not be written.
- `clock_unusable`: The system clock is outside the range a Snapshot can record.
- `history_unreadable`: The Root's history could not be read.
- `body_invalid`: The request body is not the JSON this endpoint takes.
- `purge_invalid`: `purge` is neither `true` nor `false`.
- `config_invalid`: The Root's configuration cannot be read, so nothing is captured on terms it does not state.
- `comparison_invalid`: `from` is not a Snapshot's identity, or `to` is neither one nor `working`.
- `format_invalid`: `format` is neither `json` nor `unified`.
- `confirmation_required`: A path of the request needs a confirmation or a resolution, or cannot be restored: nothing was written, and `paths` says what each needs.
- `resolution_invalid`: A resolution sets no answer or more than one, or names a new name that is not a bare name.
- `withheld`: The Snapshot holds no content at this path on purpose, so there is none to read or restore; `details.reason` says why.
- `job_not_found`: No job with this identity is known: none was started, or the daemon has restarted since, which forgets every job.
- `maintenance_unavailable`: No `git` a Maintenance Pass can run with is usable; `GET /v1/status` says why and how to install one.
- `maintenance_failed`: A Maintenance Pass ran and failed; `detail` holds what `git` said.
- `job_interrupted`: The daemon stopped before the job could start; nothing was done.
- `glob_invalid`: `glob` is not a pattern Forget can remove: malformed, or a negation, which names what to keep.
- `secret_opted_in`: A path the glob matches is on the secret opt-in list, which says it is to be captured, so it cannot be excluded from now on; `details.path` names it.
- `volume_mismatch`: The Root's directory is not on the volume it was registered on, so nothing is captured from or restored into it; its history is as readable as ever.
- `store_unreachable`: The Root's History Store cannot be opened or written, so nothing is captured: there is no other store to write to instead.
- `preview_busy`: A Capture Preview is already walking; one runs at a time, so this one was not started.
- `preview_invalid`: `only` is not `captured`, `excluded`, `withheld` or `unreadable`, or the preview's query is otherwise malformed.
- `preview_failed`: The Capture Preview could not be prepared; nothing was walked, and asking again may succeed.
- `dest_in_store`: The Export's destination is inside a History Store, which nothing may write into; `details.path` names it.
- `dest_unwritable`: The Export's destination cannot be written: it is not a directory, or cannot be made or written into; `details.path` names it.
- `directory_unreadable`: The directory cannot be listed; `details.path` names it.
- `query_invalid`: The search query is empty, or is not a pattern or a regular expression that can be compiled; `detail` says why.
- `search_invalid`: A content search names no Root: give `roots`, or ask for `all`.
- `unauthorized`: The loopback listener was asked without its token: no cookie a bootstrap code was exchanged for, no `Authorization: Bearer` with the token, or a bootstrap code already used.
- `host_refused`: The request's `Host` is not the loopback listener's own address with its port, which is how a page rebinding its own name to the loopback is told apart.
- `origin_refused`: The request's `Origin` is not the listener's own, nor one `ui.allowed_origins` names.
- `log_level_invalid`: A raise of the log level names a level this build does not know, or no duration, or one shorter than a second or longer than seven days.
- `token_failed`: A token or a bootstrap code could not be minted or written; the token in force is unchanged.
- `listener_unavailable`: The daemon has no loopback listener — `ui.listener` is off, or it could not bind — so there is no browser session to open and no token to rotate; `details.reason` is `off` or `failed`.
- `preference_invalid`: A preference names a value this build does not take: a `theme` other than `system`, `light` or `dark`, or a `syntax_line_limit` outside 1 to 10 000 000; nothing was stored.
- `preferences_failed`: The preferences could not be written; the ones stored before are unchanged.
- `mute_invalid`: A mute names a duration outside 1 to 1440 minutes; nothing was muted.
- `tray_invalid`: A tray's instance is not 1 to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`; nothing was recorded.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation of this occurrence.

details.description:
Machine-readable particulars — which path, which id, which limit — so a client composes its own
message instead of parsing ours.

paths.description:
With `confirmation_required`, every file of the Restore asked for and what it needs; absent
otherwise.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body as RFC 9457 prescribes.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

ReconcileRequest.description: What a client sends to reconcile a Root on demand.

oneOf.description:
`hash` reads every file, whatever the last pass observed — the one-off answer to a filesystem
whose mtimes cannot be trusted; `stat` trusts the size-and-mtime filter even where `hash` is
configured. Absent, the Root's configured mode applies.

Reconciled.description: What a Reconciliation asked for on demand did.

coarse_mtime.description:
Whether every mtime the pass saw fell on a whole second — a sign the filesystem keeps none finer,
which makes the size-and-mtime filter weaker than it looks.

hashed.description: How many files the pass read and hashed; the rest were vouched for by what the last pass saw.

observed.description: How many files the pass compared.

oneOf.description: The Snapshot the pass wrote; absent when the Working Tree matched the latest Snapshot.

RegisterRoot.description: What a client sends to register a directory.

path.description: The directory to watch. Made absolute by the daemon; not resolved through symlinks.

RegistryRecord.description: One Root the Registry holds, with its record as written.

error.description: Why its record cannot be read, when it cannot.

id.description: The Root's identity, which is its directory's name.

path.description: Where its directory is, from its record.

standing.description: `watched`, or `unwatched` for a Root whose history is kept after an unwatch.

volume.description: The identity of the volume it was registered on.

Reported.description:
A row whose owning behaviour has not been built yet.

It exists so that `status` can say "not known" instead of a comfortable default: ticket 05 forbids
the tool to look healthier than it is. Each variant below is added by the ticket that can actually
determine the fact, and adding one is an additive change to `/v1`.

RestoreIssue.description: Why a file of a Restore is not simply written.

confirm.description: The confirmation that settles it, for the four that one does.

current_mode.description: For `modes_differ`: the permission bits on disk now.

links_outside.description: For `hardlinked`: how many more names the file has outside the Root.

paths.description:
For `hardlinked`: the file's other names inside the Root. For `name_collision`: the other
Snapshot paths that are one file with it.

reason.description:
The reason: `parent_missing`, `type_change`, `hardlinked`, `overwrite_unrecoverable`,
`name_collision`, `name_invalid`, `name_case`, `modes_differ`, `type_conflict`,
`link_check_failed` or `withheld`. An open set, as error codes are.

resolution.description:
The resolution that settles it — `write`, `rename_to`, `name_case` or `modes` — for the four only
the user can answer. Neither this nor `confirm` for a path that cannot be restored at all.

snapshot_mode.description: For `modes_differ`: the Snapshot's permission bits, as a number (`384` is `0o600`).

RestoreOutcome.description: What happened to one file of a Restore.

RestoreRequest.description:
What a client sends to restore — `POST /v1/roots/{id}/restore` (ticket 47).

Restore only overwrites and creates; it never deletes. The whole request is checked before anything is
written: a path that needs a confirmation or a resolution, or cannot be restored, stops it whole.

confirm.description:
